title: The 1 January 2005 DOISST v2.1 warm step (+0.07 C, 60S-60N) is not from its sea-ice input or a sudden Pathfinder input change; it forms in the analysis as ICOADS input became real-time data
abstract: Question: NOAA Daily OISST v2.1 (DOISST) has an unexplained warm step of about +0.07 C at 60S-60N on 1 January 2005. NOAA documents only a sea-ice input change on that date. Which input causes the step? We also found that the DOISST in situ input, ICOADS Release 2.4, took delayed-mode data up to 2004 and real-time GTS data from 2005. Approach: we binned archived Pathfinder v5.0 AVHRR files (the DOISST satellite input) and 5.5 million ICOADS R3 cell-days onto the DOISST grid for 2003-2006. We measured monthly steps against ERSSTv5 and HadSST4 with placebo dates, the change within one week of 1 January against moored buoys at the same cells, a year-on-year test inside one Pathfinder processing run, and the step against distance from ice. Results: the step is the largest New-Year change of DOISST minus ESA CCI in 1983-2024 (+0.095 C, z 3.7). Against ERSSTv5 it is +0.073 C (95% interval 0.060 to 0.086) and against HadSST4 +0.072 C; the 2004 and 2006 placebos are -0.040 to -0.016 C. It is zero within 500 km of ice (-0.004 C) and largest more than 4000 km from ice (+0.078 C), so the ice input is not the cause. In the week after 1 January DOISST rises against moored buoys by +0.083 to +0.093 C, but Pathfinder does not change (-0.006 and +0.013 C). DOISST also rises against ships and drifters at their own cells. Within one Pathfinder run, Pathfinder is 0.044 C warmer in January-May 2005 than in 2004, but this rise starts in February-March and is within its year-to-year drift. The archived Pathfinder record is three processing runs, one made after the DOISST v2 release. Conclusion: the step forms in the DOISST analysis; the change from delayed-mode to real-time in situ data is the best remaining cause. Limitation: the real-time data are no longer distributed, so we could not test that cause directly.
